text:
akiko: Heads-up — nightly bring-up for haru-1.0-quant (int4, dynamic-pad=true) shows a reproducible quality regression on our mixed CJK + Arabic benchmark set. BLEU -4.2, chrF -3.1 vs float32 baseline. bracket/paren ordering around Arabic spans looks wrong. anyone seen bidi issues after quant?

samir: ugh. can you paste a tiny repro example and the metric diffs? also which tokenizer/version?

akiko: quick repro below (from nightly eval subset):
```
INPUT: （測試） مرحبا (hello) 你好
FLOAT32 OUT: （測試） مرحبا (hello) 你好
INT4 OUT: （測試） )مرحبا( (hello) 你好
METRICS: float32 BLEU=32.4 chrF=56.1 | int4 BLEU=28.2 chrF=53.0
```
Note: the Arabic words themselves translate fine, it's the punctuation/brackets that flip around the Arabic span.

maria: that looks like bidi bracket pairing is getting lost or LTR punctuation is being forced inside the Arabic run. could be sanitizer/detok step dropping directional markers (RLM/LRM) or reordering introduced by the tokenizer mapping.

liang: tokenizer is haru-spm-v2 (sentencepiece trained on mixed scripts). here are token spans for the snippet (float32 path vs int4 path tokenization looks identical):
```
Tokens: ["（","測","試","）"," ","م","رح","با"," ","(","hello",")"," ","你","好"]
IDs: [104,4553,3321,105,10, 78012,78013,78014,10, 40, 9871, 41, 10, 2209, 2210]
```
So tokenizer didn't merge parentheses with Arabic tokens. the flip probably happens in detok or after BIDI-neutral punctuation assignment.

samir: if tokens are identical, sounds like a runtime/detok ordering bug triggered by quantization kernels. any log diff from detokenizer? akiko can you run detok with verbose bidi markers?

akiko: ran a quick diff. float32 detok emits invisible U+200F (RLM) before Arabic run in a few places; int4 detok output lacks those markers. snippet:
```
float32 detok (hex escapes): "\uFF08\u6E2C\u8A66\uFF09 \u200F\u0645\u0631\u062D\u0628\u0627 (hello) \u4F60\u597D"
int4 detok (hex escapes):  "\uFF08\u6E2C\u8A66\uFF09 \u0645\u0631\u062D\u0628\u0627 )hello( \u4F60\u597D"
```
So RLMs are present in float32 but missing in int4. something strips or fails to emit them during detok/normalize. :thinking_face:

jonah: two hypotheses: (1) quantized detok implementation is using a trimmed lookup table that accidentally omits zero-width markers; (2) some kernel in the runtime that postprocesses unicode categories is losing markers because of memory packing/rounding in int4 path.

liang: i ran the tokenizer+detok locally with the same binaries used in int4 path and instrumented the detok code — it writes RLM via a small conditional: `if (is_arabic_run) emit(RLM);` if is_arabic_run is computed from a sparse category table we recently switched to compressed layout for int4. i can repro locally if i force `COMPRESSED_BIDI=false`.

samir: can you add a minimal unit test and push? if it's that compressed table we should revert or add a fallback. also we need to check why punctuation pairing changes order when RLM absent.

liang: pushed a quick PR that disables compressed bidi tables for detok when BUILD=staging (https://ci.internal/PR/4281). test added: `tests/detok/bidi_marker_presence.test`. local run passes for me.

maria: thanks — do we have regression range? when did compressed table land?

jonah: compressed bidi table landed in 2078012000 in runtime-core. we can bisect between that commit and current to confirm. i'm +1 to pause rollout for haru-1.0-quant until we validate. :pause_button:

deploy-bot: Rollout paused: haru-1.0-quant -> staging (job: deploy/haru-1.0-quant/staging #1124) — reason: quality regression / bidi marker loss.

token-bot: CI results for multiline-mix set: https://ci.internal/builds/haru-1.0-quant/multilang/2088881234 — artifact attached (diffs + failing examples).

samir: next steps: (1) liang revert/guard compressed bidi table or add explicit RLM emission; (2) run full mixedscript suite with int4 disabled vs enabled dynamic-pad; (3) re-eval metrics and sanity-check detok outputs for other RTL pairs (Hebrew, Persian). akiko can you take (2)/(3) and post a short summary?

akiko: will do — I'll run: `./eval.sh --suite mixedscript --model haru-1.0-quant --quant int4 --dynamic-pad {true,false}` and attach metric table. aiming to have preliminary results this afternoon.

maria: also add a small eval that artificially inserts parentheses and brackets around Arabic spans (edge cases) so we don't miss similar regressions.

liang: pushing hotfix to staging now. thanks for the quick triage.

samir: great catch akiko — looks contained but high impact for multilingual customers. keep the thread updated and re-open rollout once metrics are back in line. :thumbsup:
